Grand Hotel Malahide Irish EBF Fillies Juvenile Race

runners_data.name: Admired Beauty
runners_data.comment: Admired Beauty shaped well when second last time out, and with 21 days between runs she arrives here in decent order. She has run over today's trip and going before, and her rating of 78 keeps her firmly in contention despite a winless recent record.

runners_data.name: Green Sparkle
runners_data.comment: Green Sparkle has run over today's trip and going before, but a ninth last time out leaves her needing to find plenty from stall 6, and winless in recent starts, she'll need a significant step forward here.

runners_data.name: Ibelieveicanfly
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lightly raced, Ibelieveicanfly has run over today's trip and going, and her second two starts back marks her as a genuine threat from stall 14; the risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Katiraya
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Katiraya steps back up to today's trip with at least the experience of it under her belt, but an eighth last time out and a rating of 57 ranked sixth of fifteen leave her with plenty to prove from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Tyre
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts, including an eighth last time out, Siege Of Tyre faces a stiff task here — our figures rank her eighth of fifteen — though she has run over today's trip before and 24 days between runs suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Speckles
runners_data.comment: Speckles has run over today's trip and going before and, drawing from a rating of 71 that ranks her third of 15, she shapes as a leading threat fresh off a 21-day break; the concern is that sixth last time out leaves her yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Voice Of You
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Voice Of You nonetheless appeals as a leading danger here — she has experience over today's trip, returns fit after 31 days, and her rating ranks her fourth of fifteen in the field. The fifth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Chattering Classes
runners_data.comment: Chattering Classes makes her debut here carrying 125 lb from stall 8, completely unexposed and open to any amount of improvement — a debut filly with everything still to prove and potentially anything to offer.

runners_data.name: Darlene
runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, Darlene makes her debut carrying 125 lb from stall 10 — lightly raced profiles like hers leave plenty of questions unanswered, but also plenty of room to improve on whatever she shows here.

runners_data.name: Miss Hong Kong
runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, Miss Hong Kong makes her debut from stall four carrying 125 lb — an open-to-improvement type with everything still to prove and potentially plenty in hand.

runners_data.name: Popped
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore completely unexposed, Popped steps into the unknown from stall five carrying 125 lb — with no form to dissect, she remains an open book with improvement ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Rathbran Lady
runners_data.comment: Rathbran Lady makes her debut from stall 2 carrying 125 lb — unraced and therefore unexposed, she is an open-to-improvement unknown whose ceiling remains entirely untested.

runners_data.name: Suomenlinna
runners_data.comment: Suomenlinna makes her racecourse debut from stall 11 carrying 125 lb — unraced and entirely unexposed, she is open to any amount of improvement and could be anything on first asking.

runners_data.name: Torvella
runners_data.comment: Torvella makes her debut carrying 125 lb from stall one, completely unexposed and open to any amount of improvement — watch for her to show plenty on first appearance.

races.name: Sheehy Motors Volkswagen Handicap

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer for Aidan Oliver who finds this course and distance combination familiar; 22 days since last run is fine, bit visor worn, but a career OR of 98 means he is competing off a career-high mark and needs everything to go perfectly from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Highway Rat did post a second three starts back, but unplaced last time out is a concern; experience over today's trip and going helps, and 22 days off suggests he's ready, though he carries 140 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Sam Coen claims 5lb on a mare who has placed twice at this trip on Good ground in her last two runs; 65 days off is the concern, though her excellent sim-going record (12/15 applicable runs) suggests the fast conditions are ideal — she will be held up and needs a clear run late.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in her last two starts, Gazelle d'Or arrives here with the form to make her mark, and she has run over today's trip and going before. The 65-day absence is worth monitoring, but her consistent placed efforts give her solid claims from stall 11 carrying 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap fitted and a busy 8yo who has been in consistent form, placing third twice in his last five on Good ground at this trip; hold-up style means he is reliant on the pace being strong enough to reel in, and sim-going record of 13/15 is the most compelling surface stat in the race.
runners_data.comment: Erosandpsyche ran a bold race to finish second last time out and has run over today's distance and going before, making him a leading contender from stall 3; the concern is he remains winless in recent starts and will need to convert that placed form.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: A genuinely in-form 4yo who has won twice in recent starts and placed in between; hold-up rider Jared Huggan claims 10lb and she carries 136lbs, but two wins from five on similar going and a sharp 5f trip suit her accelerating style.
runners_data.comment: Sarahmae has winning form in her recent starts — a winner four and five starts back — but has drifted to fifth last time out, suggesting she's finding this level tougher; she has run over today's trip and going, and 136 lb is the key ask.

runners_data.name: Headmaster
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on a horse whose true style is hold-up, but the map shows him in midfield because there are too many genuine closers for the rear positions — he may race closer to the pace than ideal, and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers his chance; his best form has come over 6-7f rather than this minimum trip.
runners_data.comment: Returned unplaced last time out after a runner-up effort two starts back, though he did score three starts back; experience over today's trip and going helps, but 135 lb from stall 14 is no gimme at a mark of 93.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: David Egan on a lightly-weighted 3yo who won over this exact course and distance last time; a genuine prominent type who gets her own position in this field and whose Good-ground record here makes her the most straightforward profile in the race — the 3lb penalty is absorbed into the OR adjustment.
runners_data.comment: Ipanema Queen comes into this in excellent nick, winning last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going — the main risk is that she must shoulder 134 lb from stall 8, which could test her stamina late on.

runners_data.name: Arugam Bay
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman (7lb claim) partners a 3yo who has been absent 126 days and whose recent form on this going is modest (6 out of 7 applicable runs off the board); the long lay-off combined with the sharp step back into 5f handicap company is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Arugam Bay has run over today's trip and showed real ability with back-to-back wins four and five starts back, but three subsequent disappoints culminating in a ninth last time out raise questions, and 126 days off the track adds further uncertainty despite the handy draw from stall two.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner for Patrick Magee, equipped with a tongue-strap and set to be ridden by Colin Keane who will aim for an uncontested lead; her last Curragh win came over this exact course and distance on Good ground 16 days ago, making her the dominant pace figure.
runners_data.comment: Rosie Frith won three starts back but has since posted back-to-back fourths, suggesting she's consistent without quite firing; she has run over today's trip and going, and 16 days since her last run keeps her fresh, though 131 lb is a stern weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Chicago Call
runners_data.note: A JP Murtagh-trained 3yo trained to race prominently but whose recent form figures of 5-6-7-8 are deteriorating; prominent style is genuine but the downward OR trajectory and Good-to-Firm going following previous runs on Soft are both mild concerns.
runners_data.comment: Chicago Call has run over today's trip and going, and his speed rating of 85 backs his claims from stall five, 16 days on from his last outing; the concern is a winless recent sequence of five starts.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Carries the blinkers and hood combination (tp) and was third last time over 6f on Good before a recent win over 5f; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and the horse's sim-going record of 14/15 is outstanding — a genuine prominent type whose course-and-distance profile makes him a key player.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Genesis faces a stiff task from stall ten carrying 125 lb, and a sixth last time out does little to inspire confidence; he has won in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, but he needs a significant upturn to factor.

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: 170 days off the track is significant, and all five recent career runs are on Standard artificial ground at The Curragh's all-weather track — this will be her first start on turf in her recent string and Good-to-Firm conditions represent a meaningful unknown; her prominent style could suit if fit.
runners_data.comment: Prairie Girl has back-to-back wins in her recent record but was unplaced last time out and returns after 170 days off — a combination that makes her hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings. She has run over today's trip, at least.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: A 6yo prominent runner with a modest sim-going record (8/15) who has been gelded and has shown one win on a Good surface at 5f; trained by Patrick McKenna who has no runners in the past 14 days — straightforward type but OR of 79 leaves him at the bottom of the weights.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Grey has struggled for consistency in recent starts — a winner four runs back but ninth and seventh since, then fourth last time out — and ranks 12th of 14 on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights despite having experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Finika
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer for John James Feane whose three-run form of 1-3-11 shows a rapid regression, though all three runs have come on Good ground at the Curragh and she carries only 120lbs; because the field is overloaded with closers she has been mapped into midfield — her true rear-of-field role is compressed, which tempers her chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Finika faces a stiff task, though she does arrive in decent nick — a winner last time out — and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Ran just 6 days ago and faces a quick turnaround for JA Stack; her natural prominent style has been pushed into the midfield map because the prominent berths are taken, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means she is unlikely to get the position she needs — the short recovery window adds a further layer of caution.
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid second last time out, but her two starts before that yielded finishes of eighth and seventh, making consistency the question mark. Has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 92 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark implies.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field over the Curragh's straight 5f on Good to Firm ground, and with Colin Keane aboard she is likely to stride clear from the gates and set a measured, uncontested tempo rather than a suicidal gallop. The prominent positions will be heavily congested from the outset, with Ipanema Queen, Arugam Bay, Chicago Call, Genesis, Prairie Girl, and Cuban Grey all wanting to race close to the pace — that six-horse scrum creates serious traffic and interference risks between the 2f and 3f markers. Focaccia is a natural prominent type forced into a midfield map position because the prominent berths are already oversubscribed, while Headmaster and Finika are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the rear of the field will be less stacked with finishers than it appears. The field holds more prominent-hunting types than can all secure their preferred position, and Rosie Frith is the one horse almost certain to get hers; with a sustainable, uncontested lead on fast ground over a sharp 5f, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can sidestep the prominent-group traffic and pick off a front-runner who has controlled her own fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosie Frith Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith breaks well and settles into an uncontested lead, controlling every fraction without pressure from the prominent group.
scenarios.body: Colin Keane steers Rosie Frith to an unchallenged lead and, on quick ground that rewards horses who avoid the midfield scrimmage, she conserves enough energy to hold on through the final furlong. The prominent runners burn energy jostling for position and arrive too late, making a front-runner who controls her own race the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-group scramble creates a moderately strong pace and the closers find a clean passage down the stands rail or centre.
scenarios.body: The Highway Rat, Gazelle d'Or, Erosandpsyche, and Sarahmae sit last or second-last but benefit from the pace injection caused by six horses competing for prominent spots, getting a true run into open ground in the final 2f on fast going. This is the scenario where the deepest-sitting hold-up horses are rewarded, provided their jockeys find clear daylight early enough to launch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse breaks cleanly ahead of the pack and tracks Rosie Frith at a comfortable distance without getting boxed in.
scenarios.body: A single prominent runner who avoids the early traffic — most likely Ipanema Queen or Genesis given their recent Good-ground form — settles just off the leader's shoulder and has enough left to collar Rosie Frith in the final 100 yards. This shape suits horses whose natural prominent style is genuinely their own rather than a map redistribution, and who have the fitness to sustain it on fast ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-group congestion causes significant interference or checks and several runners are shuffled back, flattening pace and randomising the finish.
scenarios.body: With multiple horses forced out of their natural positions, the race loses its anticipated shape entirely and a horse like Finika or Focaccia — natural pace types racing off a low OR — benefits from the disorder by finding an unexpected gap. This low-probability scenario is discounted because it relies on redistributed runners performing outside their mapped role, but a chaotic 5f sprint can occasionally produce exactly this result.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Ipanema Queen, Arugam Bay, Chicago Call, Genesis, Prairie Girl, and Cuban Grey all want the same early positions behind Rosie Frith, making a check or interference incident between the 3f and 2f poles a genuine danger for anything caught in the scramble.

Rosie Frith's early break — if Colin Keane gets her away cleanly and she crosses to the rail uncontested, the entire race shape locks in around her; watch the first 2f to see whether any prominent runner pushes into her space, as that would immediately change the pace dynamic.

Prairie Girl's turf debut concern — 170 days off, all recent form on Standard surface, now racing on Good-to-Firm turf; if she breaks sharply and adds to the prominent congestion she could compound the traffic problem, but if she is unable to handle the going she may drift back at a critical moment.

Focaccia's quick turnaround — ran only 6 days ago and is a natural prominent type forced into midfield; watch whether Andrew Slattery attempts to push forward early to reclaim her preferred position, which would intensify the prominent-group logjam.

Sarahmae hold-up run — she carries the joint-top weight for hold-up horses (136lbs with a 10lb claim reducing the impact) and her two recent wins suggest she is in career form; the key watch point is whether Jared Huggan secures a clean passage down the stands side in the final 2f when the prominent group spreads across the track.

races.name: FBD Hotels And Resorts Phoenix Sprint Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old in excellent current form — two wins from his last five on Good/Good to Firm and a course-and-distance victory last time out; 21 days since that win keeps him fresh, and his clean jumping style from prominent makes him the ideal Big Mojo shadow.
runners_data.comment: Big Gossey arrives in fine heart — a winner two starts back and runner-up last time out, with experience over today's trip and going and a 21-day break suggesting he's ready to fire; the main risk is whether 133 lb blunts his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed pace-setter whose uncontested lead is the defining structural fact of this race; sim-going strike rate of 13/15 on similar ground is strong, though recent finishes of 10-8-7 before his last win suggest the OR-113 ceiling may be tested if the pace is too generous to closers.
runners_data.comment: Big Mojo landed a win five starts back and brings distance-and-going experience into this, with our rating of 114 topping the field — the risk is his recent form has been modest, with four unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance on Good ground earlier this season and Colin Keane retains the ride — genuine prominent racer who finds himself pushed wider in the pack because the field is overloaded with pace types, but his 5f win and bounce-back potential from a 22-day break mean he is not without claims if he can find daylight.
runners_data.comment: Beaten last time out and ranked bottom of five on our figures, Bodhi Bear faces a stiff task off 133 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and that winning burst — a first three starts back — shows he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Bucanero Fuerte
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's five-year-old carries a form string of 7-7546 that inspires little confidence at this level; a natural front-runner by inclination, he is squeezed out of his preferred slot here, and his best going figures come on Firm rather than Good to Firm, compounding the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bucanero Fuerte nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at 22 days fresh he arrives in good order; drawn four carrying 133 lb, his rating of 108 marks him as a lively outsider capable of outrunning his recent finishing positions.

runners_data.name: James's Delight
runners_data.note: Clive Cox has two winners from 22 in the past fortnight and McMonagle is an obvious booking, but 78 days off, a natural prominent style shunted to the rear by a field packed with pace types, and only 6/15 in similar-going handicaps all combine to make this the most structurally challenged runner in the race.
runners_data.comment: James's Delight shaped well when third last time out and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, carrying 133 lb from stall 5; the main concern is a 78-day absence that leaves fitness on trust.

races.paceDynamic: Big Mojo is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners over 6f on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh, Tom Marquand can expect to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop without serious challenge for the lead. The field is unusually pace-loaded for its size — Bucanero Fuerte, Bodhi Bear, and James's Delight are all natural prominent types who cannot all occupy their preferred ground, meaning at least two will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal, creating a compressed midpack behind a single pace-setter. Big Gossey, a reliable prominent-to-handy performer, is the one runner most likely to track Big Mojo cleanly without sacrificing position. The race shape strongly favours the horse who can sit closest to a measured, uncontested pace and produce a clean turn-of-foot, making prominent-to-handy runners who secure a position directly behind the leader the primary beneficiaries; true hold-up tactics are structurally disadvantaged here because there is no genuine tempo injection to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Big Mojo Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Big Mojo leads unchallenged and sets a fair but not suicidal clip, allowing Marquand to dictate every fraction.
scenarios.body: Big Mojo establishes an uncontested lead and, with no rival willing to burn early energy to close him down, converts a prominent style into a wire-to-wire success on Good to Firm ground where his form figures read best. Horses racing behind a single, unhurried pace-setter on fast ground rarely have enough cover to mount a late assault, and Big Mojo's recent course form and high sim-going strike rate support the view that this surface suits.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Big Mojo's pace proves just comfortable enough for a well-placed tracker to reel him in across the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Big Gossey, travelling prominently and freshened by a 21-day break with a strong recent record on this going, is ideally placed to challenge if Big Mojo's stride shortens late. A nine-year-old who has won over this course and distance on similar ground, Big Gossey's ability to maintain rhythm from a handy position makes him the most natural beneficiary should the leader flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Reshuffled Prominent Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — Bucanero Fuerte or Bodhi Bear — overcomes their compromised position to storm through.
scenarios.body: Racing outside their natural slot carries a meaningful cost in a five-runner sprint where every length of ground lost early is hard to recover, but Bodhi Bear's course-and-distance win and Colin Keane's ability to find a run from an awkward position give this scenario some credibility. Bucanero Fuerte's recent form string of 7-7546 is less persuasive, though a clean break and an uncontested early move could restore his position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: James's Delight Closes From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If James's Delight, mapped to a hold-up role out of necessity, produces an exceptional turn of foot from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: A 78-day absence and a natural prominent style redistributed to the back of a small field make this a low-probability outcome, though McMonagle's excellent big-race record means the execution risk is limited. James's Delight would need a slow early pace combined with rivals tying each other up — conditions that are structurally unlikely given Big Mojo's uncontested lead.

watchPoints.text: Big Mojo's early sections bear watching — if Marquand exploits the unchallenged lead to slow the race to a crawl, the compressed pack behind could close rapidly in the final furlong, turning an apparent control scenario into a sprint finish for the chasers.

Big Gossey's draw and early movement deserve attention at the start — if he can tuck directly onto Big Mojo's quarters without burning energy, he becomes dangerous; any wide, flat position tracking from outside would erode his late challenge.

Bodhi Bear's first 100 yards will reveal whether Colin Keane attempts to push forward and reclaim a prominent position — if he does, it increases the chance of a contested early lead and raises Big Mojo's effort level considerably.

James's Delight's return from 78 days is the significant unknown; Cox horses can be fit fresh, but the redistribution to a hold-up role in a race without genuine pace compression is structurally unkind and any sign of ring-rustiness will end his chance immediately.

Going described as Good to Firm throughout the card — any additional drying by the 3:25 slot could sharpen sectionals further and increase the advantage of the horse most comfortable bowling along on fast ground, which points back to Big Mojo's sim-going record of 13/15.

races.name: Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Dropped in class here after a flat seventh in the Prix Morny, but wins at 5f and 6f on Good ground give him strong positional options off a prominent pitch; Ronan Whelan will be expected to slot just behind the front-runners and he has the Curragh form to fire.|
runners_data.comment: Carry The Flag won two starts back and brings solid experience over today's trip and conditions, with 131 lb and stall one the main questions from draw 1; if he bounces back from a modest latest effort, he looks a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount holds the highest recent form line (1-0-1), with both wins coming over this exact track and trip on similar going; faces a tactical battle to secure the lead against three rivals of similar profile, but quality suggests he can hold his position.|
runners_data.comment: Celeron has won two of his last three starts, most recently striking 22 days ago, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 131 lb from stall eight, that weight is worth noting, but his current form makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Folsom Blues
runners_data.note: A prominent runner who has only once raced over 6f and showed raw speed winning over 7f soft; steps into Group 1 company against faster rivals, and his previous 6f run was a third-place effort on Good — he may find the headlong pace too intense to land a blow.|
runners_data.comment: Folsom Blues arrives in fair recent form — a winner two starts back and second last time out — and has run over today's trip, but our rating of 88 ranks him bottom of the field, making him hard to fancy at the weights carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: King Of Cloughan
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good last time, giving him solid form credentials at exactly the right trip and going; sits handy without being a confirmed front-runner, meaning the contested pace suits him perfectly if Joseph O'Brien's barn is in form (11/76 T14).|
runners_data.comment: King Of Cloughan arrives here in decent nick — second last time out after winning two starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions. Carrying 131 lb from stall three, he's competitive at a rating of 102 but faces a stiff task ranked fifth of eight.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who has won over 6f on Good going but whose trainer's T14 strike-rate of 1/13 gives little confidence; has struggled when the pace is slow but could find a true-run Group 1 tempo enabling a late rattle, making him a minor interest rather than a headline act.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and without a win in his last two starts, The Scallionator is hard to fancy ranked bottom on our figures; a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement, but the 131 lb burden adds further to his task.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed front-runners whose lead position will be fiercely contested by Celeron, Sun Goddess, and Folsom Blues; the 14th-place effort at Chester suggests vulnerability when things don't go his way, and being pushed off his lead by rivals of higher class is a real risk.|
runners_data.comment: Tribeca shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, he arrives fit on 22 days' rest with experience over today's trip and going — the unplaced effort sandwiched between those runs is the one query to resolve.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount is the X-factor — two wins over this course and trip on identical going, and her filly's allowance gives her a weight edge over the colts; if Moore gets a clean break and settles her just in front or on the speed, she is the most consistent finisher in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Sun Goddess arrives in fine nick — a winner last time out and again three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going — though the 43-day absence is the one question mark over her readiness.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: A horse of genuine early pace whose last three runs include two impressive wins at shorter; pushed to the rear of the pace map due to redistribution — her true style is prominent, not hold-up, so any chance is best realised through a forward move, and the T14 rate of 3/10 is solid for Twomey.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and she has winning form in recent starts, but an eighth two starts back blots the copybook. She has run over today's trip and going, and returns fit on 15 days' rest, though 128 lb and a ranking of sixth of eight suggest plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Celeron, Tribeca, Folsom Blues, and Sun Goddess all carry strong front-running credentials, guaranteeing a contested, high-tempo gallop from the outset over 6f on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh — a combination that will stretch this juvenile field from the first furlong. With four legitimate lead horses unable to all secure their preferred position, the early scrimmage will almost certainly produce a genuinely searching pace rather than a controlled, tactical crawl, placing a serious premium on resolution and class in the closing stages. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their positions cleanly, and Celeron (highest OR, proven 6f winner) and Sun Goddess (Ryan Moore, Aidan O'Brien) are best placed to actually secure rail-side berths, while Folsom Blues and Tribeca are most likely to be shuffled off their ideal spot. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-pressing runner with tactical speed and stamina to sustain a challenge through a hot pace rather than a pure hold-up finisher, meaning runners like Carry The Flag and King Of Cloughan, who can sit handy without burning energy at the front, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Presser Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the four lead horses fight for position early and the pace is truly end-to-end, leaving a prominent pressing horse to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The blistering early fractions will drain the true front-runners late, and a horse that sits just off the lead under a cool hand will sprint past spent rivals in the final furlong on this flat, fast Curragh surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Celeron Controls and Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If Celeron secures a comfortable lead without serious pressure and is allowed to dictate a measured tempo.
scenarios.body: Murphy's Group 1 experience gives Celeron the edge in an early contest for the front, and if he finds a rhythm unchallenged he can produce the turn of foot that powered his two wins at this course and distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Exploit Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that the entire lead group ties up, allowing a horse to rattle home from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Velozee, while repositioned on the pace map, does retain raw finishing speed, and The Scallionator has previously shown ability to close from a stalking position when the tempo is brutal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sun Goddess Leads, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Ryan Moore sends Sun Goddess to the front early and the opposition fails to match her finishing effort after a tactical race.
scenarios.body: Sun Goddess's consistent Good-to-Firm form (2W from 4 runs), Group-level class, and a confident booking from Moore make her a threat if she can secure a smooth lead and control the fractions.

watchPoints.text: Celeron and Sun Goddess are both confirmed front-runners drawn in a field of four pace-setters — watch the first furlong for any collision or crowding that disrupts the race's early order and potentially changes the complexion entirely.

Velozee is mapped to hold up but her natural style is prominent; if she contests for the lead instead of settling, the field's already intense pace rises further, compounding the risk to every front-runner's stamina in the final 2f.

Folsom Blues has only one run over 6f in form and that was a placing rather than a win; his finishing speed relative to this Group 1 field is unproven, and Dylan Browne McMonagle may find him outpaced in the final furlong if the gallop is truly hot.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed in the going report for the 4:00 race) rewards horses with clean, efficient action; any runner who showed preference for softer surfaces in their history — notably Folsom Blues (7f win on Soft) — may not reproduce their best here.

The Curragh's flat, straight 6f is unforgiving for horses that lose early position — King Of Cloughan's ability to travel prominently without leading makes him a horse to track through the early stages if the lead group goes off too hard.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Has a solid record at 6f on good ground (2nd twice at this trip in recent form) and Ronan Whelan retains the ride; at 8 years old this gelding knows his job and often produces a sustained late rattle, but the crowded hold-up pack means he may not find the unobstructed path his finishing style demands.
runners_data.comment: Go Athletico has been placed three times in his last six starts — second last time out and a second three starts back — and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround having run over today's distance and going; winless in recent starts, he nonetheless heads the ratings and commands respect off 141 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: Returned a 2nd and a 4th in similar conditions earlier in the campaign and Scott McCullagh has a positive record on the horse; the 63-day break is a question mark, though the trainer has limited 14-day evidence and this type often needs a run to find full momentum late.
runners_data.comment: Gerrit's Gem has run over today's trip and his rating of 80 makes him a live contender among these fifteen, but a 63-day absence and a winless run of five recent starts — the latest a seventh — leave him needing to find form quickly.

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Edward Lynam's sprinter has a win at 6f on good ground in his recent history and is arguably the most course-proven runner in the race; a true hold-up horse who will be squeezed into a midfield berth by the traffic of closers, meaning his finishing kick could be wasted if he cannot get daylight down the straight.
runners_data.comment: Jon Riggens arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip, while our rating of 79 puts him in the mix; the main concern is the 63-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old stepping up to 6f having won over 5f on good ground — the trip extension is the key question — and Shane Foley gives this runner a significant booking upgrade; the form figures include a latest run of 8th over 5f which may just reflect the trip being too sharp.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Cry won two starts back but has struggled either side of that, finishing eighth last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 134 lb from stall 13, he needs to find more consistency to make a serious mark from a rating of 78.

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: Consistent at staying in the first five across every recent start, all on good or good-to-firm ground, and the 6-day turnaround suggests connections are confident in fitness; W J Lee rides and this horse's repeated placed efforts without winning may point to a horse that finds one too good, though the form makes it a natural each-way contender in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but a second two runs back shows he can threaten; has run over today's trip and going, though six days between runs is a quick turnaround and carrying 131 lb from stall 14 adds to his task.

runners_data.name: Nazario
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who is expected to control this race from the front; J P Murtagh's 3-year-old has worn a hood (tp) and has found a level of consistency at 6f on good ground, though his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that his natural role is prominent rather than commanding, and if pressed he could capitulate.
runners_data.comment: Nazario arrives on the back of consecutive fourths, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 81 puts him right among the principals here — the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a mare with three placed efforts in her last four at 6f on good ground — the form is genuinely solid; her natural position is off the pace but with so many closers in the field she will end up mid-division, potentially closer than ideal but not necessarily disadvantaged if Murphy makes use of the position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, though a second three starts back and third four starts back show she's capable of mixing it at this level; the back-to-back fourths lately are a concern, and from stall 8 off 128 lb she'll need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-calibre booking for a horse that has been remarkably consistent at 5f, scoring once on soft and placing repeatedly; stepping to 6f is the primary concern here, and although he will be forced closer than his natural rear position, the extra furlong may actually suit if he settles early.
runners_data.comment: Nouvel Espoir won three starts back but has posted two fourth-place finishes since, and that recent consistency at the minors is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and 127 lb from stall 15 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: The "fades in finish" flag is significant — this 3-year-old has a clear pattern of weakening in the closing stages on good ground at 6f, and Gary Carroll will need a very specific run of events for him to hold on; flagged as a horse who tends to race too freely and pay for it late, which is amplified when shuffled into midfield rather than settling at the back.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Has won over 6f on good ground and wears a hood (tv), suggesting he can be keen; Chris Hayes is an experienced handler for a horse out of his natural position at the rear, and the 18-day turnaround keeps him fresh, but the form string (784803) reflects inconsistency that makes him hard to rely on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mint Man does offer a sliver of hope — third last time out suggests he retains some ability, though a string of unplaced efforts beyond that keeps confidence measured; he has run over today's trip and returns after 18 days off.

runners_data.name: Yutori
runners_data.note: Has raced almost exclusively at 7f–10f on Flat/AW surfaces and the switch to 6f turf on good-to-firm is a steep change in context; only 1 from 7 in similar going conditions, and a 177-day absence compounds the concerns — this horse looks significantly out of role on multiple counts, not just positionally.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning from 177 days off the track, Yutori faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 126 lb; a second two starts back offers a flicker of hope, and she has run over today's trip, but her rating of 64 leaves her well held on these figures.

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old veteran with 12 career wins at the track but the recent form figures (13, 9, 5, 3, 12) are erratic; Wesley Joyce claims 3lbs on a lightly-weighted runner but the horse is naturally a hold-up type being pushed forward by field congestion, and the last time it ran truly prominently it emptied late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with unplaced efforts in two of her most recent three, Aurora Nova faces a stiff task ranked 12th of 15 on our figures; she does bring distance-and-going experience and a return after 29 days, but little else points her way.

runners_data.name: Beat The Devil
runners_data.note: The distance history is alarming — this horse has recent form at 8f to 18f and now drops sharply to 6f, which represents a major trip reduction without any obvious turf sprint pedigree; the going figures (3 from 15 in similar conditions) confirm this is a deeply unfamiliar context and the redistribution into midfield merely adds to the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of these 15 on our figures, Beat The Devil is hard to fancy after an unplaced effort last time; he has run over today's trip before and 28 days' rest at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Caislean Ni Cuan
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins's 3-year-old has three starts, all at 7f on good ground, and steps down 1f in trip for the first time; the prominent style suits the race shape if she has natural pace for 6f, and N G McCullagh's booking is competent, though the inexperience relative to older rivals is a genuine unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — fifth last time out, seventh two starts back, and fourth three starts back — Caislean Ni Cuan faces a stiff task from stall 12 on these figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns quickly enough after just 12 days.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Patrick McGettigan's 5lb claim reduces the weight on a 5-year-old with a 2nd at 6f on good ground in his form — Charles Weld's gelding has been placed in conditions identical to today's and the prominent style means he should track Nazario without fighting for position; the OR of 58 is the lowest in the field but the style-fit to this specific race shape is among the best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a seventh and worse before that second last time out, Rosato faces a stiff ask ranked 11 of 15 on our figures — though 16 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Nazario is the one confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner sprint and, with no serious rival prepared to press hard from the gates, he should be able to control tempo from a prominent position at whatever level of pace suits his rider Rory Mulligan. The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions throughout the card — fast ground that rewards horses who travel strongly mid-race and finish off, rather than those who need soft ground to grind. The field is saturated with hold-up types: Jon Riggens, Hugo's Girl, All Hail, Nouvel Espoir, Mint Man, Yutori, Aurora Nova and Beat The Devil are all genuine closers who cannot all take up their preferred rear positions — several will be shuffled forward into unfamiliar midfield slots, reducing the effectiveness of the late burst the race shape would otherwise generate. With Nazario controlling a sustainable gallop unchallenged and a congested midfield unable to run freely to the rear, this race shape strongly favours horses who travel prominently or in the first half of the field and produce a smooth, uninterrupted run into the straight — the prominent-to-midfield profile that can track the pace without fighting for position is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nazario Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Nazario dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers get a clear passage into the Curragh straight.
scenarios.body: Nazario sets the fractions from the front with no challenger for the lead, allowing runners like Caislean Ni Cuan and Rosato to track in a position of maximum efficiency before unleashing their finishing kick on fast ground; the uncrowded lead rail rewards these horses over the congested hold-up pack who cannot split.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Finds Gap Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nazario's early pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and create a gap down the rail for a hold-up type to thread through.
scenarios.body: A true closer like Go Athletico or Gerrit's Gem, given a clear split in the final furlong, could collect horses who have raced prominently and tied up on the good-to-firm ground; this shape requires precise jockeyship from Ronan Whelan or Scott McCullagh to time the run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Nazario's gallop is too conservative and a cluster of midfield horses arrive together at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A compression in the field creates a scramble from two furlongs out with horses like Lohoobb and Hugo's Girl — both consistent placers in similar conditions — able to pick off tiring leaders in the final 100 yards; the good-to-firm surface keeps the race sharp enough that only the most consistent placers profit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race shape breaks down entirely and an unconsidered runner finds an uncontested run through a gap.
scenarios.body: A horse like Nouvel Espoir or Aurora Nova, shuffled forward from their natural rear position, finds themselves racing closer than usual and simply outstays rivals who have burned energy fighting for position; this shape is low-probability precisely because so many runners are out of role and the race is unlikely to fall this chaotically.

watchPoints.text: Nazario's rider Rory Mulligan must manage the pace honestly — if he dawdles in front with 14 hold-up horses hunting him down, he risks being overwhelmed in the final furlong and turning this race into a chaotic pile-up from which any backmarker could profit.

Jon Riggens, Hugo's Girl and All Hail are genuine hold-up horses being mapped into midfield positions — watch for significant barging and interference in the first two furlongs as all three attempt to find their natural rhythm in an unusually congested mid-division.

Beat The Devil's trip reduction from 18f to 6f is extreme and bears monitoring for distress signals in the early stages — if this horse gets worked up in the preliminaries or breaks poorly, it could cause interference for nearby runners.

Yutori has not raced in 177 days and drops dramatically in trip from AW routes to a 6f turf sprint — watch market moves as any significant support would suggest the stable has done specific work for this race, otherwise treat as a likely non-factor.

Good-to-firm ground confirmed for this slot throughout the card — horses who have a CONCERN flag on fast ground would be penalised here, but every runner is tagged OK, meaning the draw and jockey positioning across a 15-runner field becomes the primary variable to watch from the stalls.

races.name: Money Back Daily Specials With Tote.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping back in trip to a flat mile on Good to Firm which suits (sim-going 2W4P); 42-day break worth noting but wears blinkers and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a quality booking; needs a genuinely run race to land his finishing effort from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Booyea has run over today's trip and going, and that runner-up finish last time out — returning after 42 days — signals he's in decent heart; the worry is he's been winless in his last five starts, suggesting a win may prove elusive again.

runners_data.name: Final Voyage
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type who showed he retains ability with a win at 10f on Good recently; 84-day absence is a significant concern, and the step back to a mile with a 7lb claimer aboard makes the task harder, though trainer JP Murtagh's 14-day strike rate of 2/17 indicates some flow.
runners_data.comment: Final Voyage landed a win three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 98 marking him out as the clear class act in this field; the 84-day absence is worth noting, but he's the one to beat from stall 4 carrying 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Genuine front-to-prominent performer who won at 7f on Good and placed over 6f on Good, making this flat mile on Good to Firm an entirely fair ask; last-time-out 13th is a worry but the two runs before it were excellent, and Scott McCullagh rides; wears headgear (p) reinforcing the forward-going profile.
runners_data.comment: Glory To Be won two starts back and was second three starts back, but has since disappointed with an unplaced effort last time; she has experience over today's distance and going, and 22 days gives her time to regroup, though 135 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed at 8f and 7f on Good/Soft and handles this mile trip; trainer Feane has a quiet 14-day book (0/3) but the horse's consistent placing record suggests he will not be far away travelling prominently.

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Strong course-and-distance profile with a win at 9f Good and a place at 8f Good at this venue; 17-day turnaround is fine, trainer Harrington in good form at T14 3/36, and Shane Foley's retention is a positive; blinkers sharpen this horse's focus from hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Dark Viper arrives on the back of a win and a second in his last two starts, giving him a clear fitness edge 17 days on, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that he looked out of sorts in the three starts prior, and 134 lb is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type whose best recent runs came over this exact trip, including a third and fourth on Good surfaces; nine-year-old form at a flat 1m on Good to Firm is fair enough, though his sim-going record of 0W1P limits confidence at the top of the market.
runners_data.comment: Howyoulikethat bounced back to finish third two starts back after a disappointing seventh, and has run over today's trip — our rating of 90 suggests he's capable of going close; the concern is he remains winless in recent starts and was unplaced last time.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form (163121) and clearly a talented filly on Good, but her natural hold-up style means she is racing out of her preferred position in this field — the genuine hold-up end is congested and she is unlikely to settle as far back as she needs; discounting her chance accordingly despite the impressive form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Summer Island faces a stiff task on ratings despite a lively recent record that includes wins latest, three and six starts back, and a second two starts back; he has run over today's trip and returns after 44 days off carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Kalir
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race who will be able to control tempo from the front; Good-to-Firm ground is fine (sim-going 1W2P on Good), though the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that as a confirmed pace-setter his position at the head of affairs is secure but his ability to quicken and hold on will be tested by the prominent group behind him.
runners_data.comment: Kalir won last time out and has run over today's trip, but his speed rating of 68 and a rank of eighth of twelve suggest he faces a stiff ask, even if 25 days between runs means he arrives fresh off that success.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Excellent recent record (14321) primarily over 10-12f, which is notably further than this mile trip; a true hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield due to field congestion, and the drop in distance combined with the positional compromise tempers expectation despite the strong form on Good going.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of 12 on our figures, Marmeladova faces a stiff ask against stronger company, and a speed rating of 73 makes her hard to fancy at the weights. That said, she has run over today's trip and arrives on the back of a win last time out.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Has won and placed at 7f on Good, so the step up to 1m is a trip query; naturally a hold-up performer but finds himself mapped forward due to the congestion of closers — the headgear (t) suggests he needs to be ridden positively, which may actually help him adapt to a more prominent role.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but only fourth last time out, Goal Exceeded brings distance and going experience to the table carrying 127 lb from stall 12; our rating of 86 suggests potential, though that recent regression gives pause.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at this trip (0W5P sim-going) and wears headgear (tp) suggesting the yard is working to sharpen him; an 8-year-old whose natural late style is compromised by field congestion at the rear, and Colin Keane's presence gives this a professional look despite the positional challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures, No More Porter faces a stiff ask here despite that eighth last time out following a run of placed efforts; has run over today's trip and the 10-day turnaround at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has placed consistently on Good at 7-8f with a win at 7f on Soft; wears hood (p) and is a genuine prominent type who will look to press into second or third position behind Kalir — the lighter weight of 119lbs is an asset in a competitive handicap field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Glitter And Glory has finished fifth, third and second in her last three starts and looks hard to fancy at the weights, though she does have experience over today's trip and going, and her last-six record does contain a win and a second.

races.paceDynamic: Kalir is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no direct rival to press him hard from the gates, he is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh's flat mile. Glory To Be, Playin Cool and Glitter And Glory are genuine prominent types who will push to track Kalir closely, giving the race a clear front group without a true pace battle erupting. The resulting shape — a genuine but unhurried gallop set by Kalir, with a cluster of prominent horses sitting within a length or two — classically favours runners who can sit just off the early pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need a truly honest tempo to generate momentum from behind. Several of the hold-up horses in this field (Summer Island, Marmeladova, Goal Exceeded, No More Porter) are true rear-of-field types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given how many others want to race in a similar area, meaning their finishing kicks may be diluted or compromised by traffic; the prominent runners and those who travel sweetly just off the pace are structurally best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalir Controls; Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Kalir secures a comfortable lead and sets an honest but unhurried pace, allowing the prominent horses to travel on the bridle.
scenarios.body: Kalir rolls along at a sustainable clip, the pace cluster of Glory To Be, Playin Cool and Glitter And Glory sit just behind him, and the race develops into a straight-line stamina test where those with positional advantage and good form on Good to Firm simply outrun the closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Dries Up; Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Kalir's lead is exceptionally slow and the prominent group overdoses on a false pace, leaving a vacuum for any genuine finisher.
scenarios.body: A crawl sets up a bunch finish into the Curragh straight, but only the truest hold-up horses who manage to find clear running will benefit; Dark Viper and Booyea, both proven on this ground and suited to coming from off a slow pace, are best positioned among the back-half types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop; Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group pushes on more assertively than expected, turning the race into a genuine test of stamina and creating ground for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace thins out the prominent group and opens a lane for closers, though this scenario relies on redistributed types like Summer Island and Marmeladova getting a clean passage from compromised positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Break; Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If a ragged start or early scrimmaging reshuffles the field and negates Kalir's positional advantage.
scenarios.body: Kalir loses his uncontested lead and the tactical picture becomes confused, with mid-division horses like Dark Viper or Final Voyage benefiting from any repositioning as the field concertinas entering the straight.

watchPoints.text: Kalir's early pace is the race-shaper — watch whether Chris Hayes sends him straight to the front without a challenge, as an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop maximises the chance of the prominent group finishing fresh and the hold-up horses being left with too much to do.

Summer Island, Marmeladova and No More Porter are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same limited rear-of-field positions; a crowded closing stretch could see legitimate finishing runs shut off — watch the draw and early positioning of all three.

Dark Viper's trainer Harrington has had three winners from 36 runs in the last 14 days and Shane Foley rides — this combination from a horse with genuine Curragh form at this trip could be the most dangerous in the prominent-to-midfield switch if the pace lifts in the straight.

Final Voyage returns from an 84-day break for the JP Murtagh stable with a 7lb claimer aboard; watch the market move for signals that the yard has this horse ready, as a fresh return to form at 10f Good suggests the ability is there if the fitness is present.

Glitter And Glory represents the Harrington yard (same as Dark Viper) and brings the lightest weight in the field at 119lbs — watch whether the apprentice Kennedy settles her prominently, as her consistent recent placing record on Good at this trip makes her a liveweight factor in the straight.
